problems: The blind guess (ladle, mallet, or torch) does not identify a plumb-line. The figure reads as a line with a small triangular wedge at the bottom, not a hanging bar with a weighted bob. The mallet alternative is the closest, but the head is not clearly rounded.
The hanging bone bar is only a thin horizontal stroke at the top, too short and faint to read as a bar. Its two ends are not clearly separated.
The labels for the left end and right end of the bar overlap each other at the top ('left end of the hanging bone bar' collides with 'right end of the hanging bone'), so neither can be read.
The stone is very small and reads as a flat triangle rather than a bob with a crown, two shoulders and a point. The crown, shoulder and tip stars are crowded together at the bottom.
The gold lines run almost exactly along the star-to-star path, so the silhouette is mostly the gold outline itself rather than a filled shape built from the stars.
The figure is upright: the bar is at the top, the cord hangs down, and the point of the stone faces down. That orientation is correct.

Key stars are placed roughly on the intended parts (bar ends, cord knot, bob crown, shoulders, tip), so the star assignment is broadly right, but the spacing at the bob is too tight to tell them apart.
output.advice: Make the hanging bar a clearly thicker horizontal bar, with the left end star (64962) and right end star (64166) at its two ends and well apart. Place the cord knot (64803) at the middle of the cord. Enlarge the stone so it reads as a bob: put the crown star (65109) at the top where the cord enters, the right shoulder (64408) and left shoulder (65936) wide apart at the sides, and the point (65535) clearly below. Move the bar-end labels so they do not overlap (one above, one below, or on opposite sides). Shorten or offset the gold lines so they trace the silhouette's outline rather than sitting on the star-to-star path, so the figure reads as a real shape.
